en.title: Stories of emigrants
en.summary: Individual journeys behind the numbers: Ellis Island, assisted passage and the Windrush.

paragraphs: Statistics show the scale of migration, but stories show its human side. This lesson follows three well-documented journeys and practises inversion after place expressions, a device used in narrative writing.

Into New York harbour sailed millions of immigrants between 1892 and 1954, and at Ellis Island each arrival was inspected by doctors and officials; most were admitted within hours, but some were sent home. After the Second World War, Australia offered assisted passage to British families, who paid only ten pounds, and they were nicknamed Ten Pound Poms. On 22 June 1948 the ship Empire Windrush docked at Tilbury, bringing about 500 passengers from the Caribbean who had been invited to help to rebuild Britain. Many of them found work in transport, health care and factories, although they met prejudice in housing and employment. Their descendants are known as the Windrush generation.

paragraphs: **1. Inversion after place or direction adverbials.** When a phrase of place begins a sentence, the verb may precede the subject. See Introduction to Grammar: Sentence structure.

blocks.html:
NormalInverted
Millions of immigrants sailed into the harbour.Into the harbour sailed millions of immigrants.
A new life awaited them there.There awaited them a new life.

paragraphs: **2. Narrative tenses combine in one account.** The past simple moves the story on, the past continuous sets the scene, and the past perfect gives earlier events. See Introduction to Grammar: Past tenses.

blocks.html:
TenseRoleExample
past simplemain eventsThe ship docked.
past continuoussceneIt was raining.
past perfectearlierThey had been invited.

items: **Assisted passage** was a scheme in which the government paid part of the cost.
**Ten Pound Pom** was a nickname, sometimes affectionate and sometimes not.
**Generation** here means a group of people who share a historical experience.

paragraphs: The Windrush scandal of 2018 revealed that some people who arrived as children had been wrongly treated as illegal immigrants. It led to an official apology and a compensation scheme.
